summary: Every paid step is reserved before the call and counted against hard ceilings in SQL: collection $0.04 per Instagram profile and $0.003 per Jev stage inside $0.25 per Prague day (cursor_limits migration :98/:104), generation $0.25 per job inside a rolling $1.00 per 24 h (daily_generation_budget :57) and 8 jobs per 24 h for all brands (durable_jobs :96). Production has spent $0.019456 in total, all collection (Apify $0.0161 on 13 Oct, Jev $0.00336 over two nights); generation has spent $0 and has 0 jobs. The guards are safe but sized for fear, not for use: the $0.25 generation reservation is about 2x the arithmetic maximum of one job ($0.13) and about 10x the expected cost ($0.023); any provider failure, including unbilled 401/429, books the full $0.25 for 24 h; the 8-job cap, shared with devShark, leaves room for exactly one regeneration per post. At 4 posts a day the pipeline costs about $3/month in model spend (Sonnet 5.5), under $1/month in collection, and $0 in rendering; Haiku, vision or five-kit pre-render change this by cents to a few dollars, so cost is not what limits quality. Apify at current caps can spend at most $7.50/month, so the $150 promotional credit (expires 2026-11-22) cannot be used by the pipeline; it needs a separate owner-approved research plan. Simplicity: 42 MARKETING_* names and 13 provider variables are read, about 20 of them for retired paths (n8n, staging pilots, bridge, manual run); two retired entry points (/api/marketing/n8n and /api/marketing/dneskai/collect) can still trigger paid work when their secrets are set, and approval-notification.ts still runs on every approval. Docs disagree on plans: scaling.md says Vercel Hobby and Supabase Free and that model cost was never measured; Quorum records Apify Starter $22.99 and a $24 limit while the account reports a $244 cap plus $150 promo.

impact.statement: No money lost today, but the reservation, not the spend, is what the $1 ceiling sees: it blocks variants and regeneration long before real cost matters, and it overstates failures 2x. Fixing it lets the same $1 ceiling admit 7 concurrent jobs instead of 4.

findings.recommendation: Owner decision (rule 9: never change a reservation silently): reserve reservationFor(attemptInput) x remaining attempts (~$0.13 worst) instead of the flat $0.25, keeping $0.25 as the schema ceiling. Show reserved vs spent in Chyby a náklady.

truth.evidence: generation.ts:376 passes budget.maxCostUsd (0.25) to admitPaidCall; worker-runtime.ts:86 sends it as p_reservation; SQL:57 refuses when spent+0.25>ceiling, SQL:61-62 keeps greatest(reserved). Arithmetic max 2x(20000x2+2500x10)/1e6=$0.13 is right. But marketing_dneskai_generation_spent (SQL:27-38) counts a finished job (review/failed with a numeric usage) at its RECORDED cost, not the reservation; only running/reconciliation jobs and ambiguous failures (generation.ts:363-364, which books max(...,0.25)) count $0.25. Validation failures book real cost. So the flat reservation limits only concurrent unsettled jobs (one generation per tick already caps that at ~1), not sequential variants.
truth.correctedClaim: The ledger reserves the job's whole maxCostUsd ($0.25, ~2x the $0.13 arithmetic maximum) for each running job and for ambiguous failures; finished jobs count at their recorded cost, so the flat reservation mainly overstates ambiguous failures and caps unsettled jobs at four.
